title: Input and output
lesson:
`input("question ")` shows the question, waits for the person to type something and press Enter, and gives back what they typed **as a string**, always, even if they typed a number. So to do maths with it, convert it: `age = int(input("Age? "))`.

For output, **f-strings** are the cleanest way to mix text and values. Put an f before the quote and values in curly brackets:

```
name = "Amina"
kg = 12.5
print(f"{name} picked {kg} kg")
```

You can format numbers inside the brackets: `{price:.2f}` shows 2 decimal places, `{big:,}` adds thousands commas.

A program that asks, works something out and answers is the simplest useful program there is: a calculator, a converter, a quiz. Almost every program is that pattern, just bigger.

example.code:
name = input("What is your name? ")
year = int(input("What year were you born? "))
age = 2026 - year
print(f"Hello {name}, you turn {age} this year.")
print(f"Price: {1234.5:,.2f} KSh")
notes: f-string puts the values in the sentence.

exercises.title: Greeting
exercises.prompt: Ask for the person's name and their village, then print: Habari NAME from VILLAGE!
hints: Two input() calls, saved in two variables.
exercises.solution:
name = input("Name? ")
village = input("Village? ")
print(f"Habari {name} from {village}!")

exercises.title: Shillings to dollars
exercises.prompt: Ask how many Kenyan shillings, and the rate (shillings per dollar). Print the dollars with exactly 2 decimals, like: 1300 KSh = 10.00 USD
hints: The rate can have decimals: use float(...) for it.
dollars = ksh / rate, and {dollars:.2f} shows 2 decimals.
exercises.solution:
ksh = int(input("Shillings? "))
rate = float(input("Rate? "))
print(f"{ksh} KSh = {ksh / rate:.2f} USD")

exercises.title: Area of a plot
exercises.prompt: Ask for a plot's length and width in metres (they can have decimals). Print the area in square metres with 1 decimal, and in acres with 3 decimals (1 acre = 4046.86 m²). Format: Area: 1200.0 m2 = 0.297 acres
exercises.solution:
l = float(input("Length? "))
w = float(input("Width? "))
area = l * w
print(f"Area: {area:.1f} m2 = {area / 4046.86:.3f} acres")

quiz.q: What type does input() give back?
quiz.why: Always a string; convert it yourself.

quiz.q: age = input("Age? ") then age + 1. What happens if they type 20?
choices: TypeError: can't add str and int
quiz.why: age is the text "20"; convert with int first.

cards.q: How do you read a whole number from the person?

cards.a: An f before the quote; values in {curly brackets}.

bridge: `input("question ")` always returns text; wrap it in `int()` or `float()`. f-strings format output: `f"{name} has {kg:.1f} kg"`.
explain: Explain input and output to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up (not one from the lesson).
